addendum: R4 (review response: embedding quality of codeword messages)
status: LOCKED before running. Supplementary measurement; H1-H4 verdicts and the base protocol are unchanged.
question: Does embedding BCH16 codewords (or PAD16 messages) instead of random 32-bit messages change the image quality of WAM watermarking?
data: reserve images, COCO val2017 indices 4500-4999 (500); already used by E3/E4 (stated in the report); list sha256 must equal image_lists_sha256.reserve in configs/protocol_v5_lock.json
checkpoint: wam_coco.pth (sha256 from configs/protocol_v5_lock.json), WAM params.json (scaling_w 2.0, scaling_i 1.0, JND)
preprocessing: torchvision Resize((256,256)) then WAM default_transform, as in the base protocol

sets.BCH16: extended BCH(32,16) codewords of random 16-bit IDs
sets.PAD16: 16-bit random ID + the E3 fixed key (seed 20261104)

measurements.full: for each of the 5 messages: WAM.embed on the whole image; quality between the original and the watermarked image; per-image value = mean over the 5 messages
measurements.composite: the 5 watermarked images pasted into the 5 checkerboard squares (WAM Sec. 5.5 layout, k = 5); quality between the original and the composite
measurements.range: images mapped back to [0, 1] with WAM unnormalize_img and clamped; float values, no 8-bit rounding
measurements.PSNR: 10 log10(1 / MSE) over all pixels and channels, data range 1

statistics: image-paired percentile bootstrap, 10,000 resamples, seed 20261006, two-sided 98.75%
decision_supplementary: full-image PSNR, BCH16 - RAW: 'no quality difference' if the whole 98.75% interval lies inside +-0.1 dB; otherwise report the difference and add it to the limitations. The same rule is reported (not decided) for PAD16 - RAW and for the composite.
reference: WAM paper reports PSNR 38.3 dB for WAM (App. G.2, Table 8; its own evaluation protocol); our values are at 256x256 and shown alongside for orientation only
document_rule: add a quality table to section 5.8 and one sentence to the discussion/limitations; if equivalent, state that codeword embedding does not change WAM's image quality within +-0.1 dB
